chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Great advances happen accidentally
summary: Dance and Clarke talk about how timing and accidents, controlled by capable people, produce great inventions.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Uh-huh. There's a thing -- there's a time element for people.
You know? And everybody gets green -- the green fields for the same people.
So it's -- well, not exactly at the
same. There are those right in at the start of it.
And those that come right in.
That come in, yeah, who are able to fit in.
That's right. That's right. And those that grow up into it.
But it's just a -- it's cultivation, isn't it.

But it's funny how you -- you know, with most all great inventions and things that have happened in the world that improve people's standard of living or their thinking, it seems to happen accidentally. To me it does. You know, it happens, when someone tries to do something and studies it, it doesn't seem to work exactly like he would like it to work, like he had figured it out.
It always works in a different way.
He's looking for one thing and something else comes up.
But sometimes he's looking enough and capable to control it.
And that's what makes a great man out of him.
But sometimes thing are going not exactly like he wants them to go. Like he says, 'I expected this to be this and this to be that.'
That's what makes a great man, I think.

Because I don't think things really happen, really, like they're intended to. You know, when someone builds, maybe he builds an engine, or whatever he builds, there's something about it that the unexpected always happens.
It's some little thing that's missing.
And finally he -- he discovers this missing link, you know.
He says, 'Well, it should work, but it doesn't. Now what's --,' you know?
Then what he -- this missing link always comes about accidentally.
And when he's not even expecting it.
Yes, and it's very strange, isn't it?
Yeah, it is, but usually things happen like that.
I mean things are not straightforward.
And there isn't a straightforward price tag on things, is there.
That's very funny. So you can even say, you know, that old saying about an ill wind blows no-one -- or whatever that is, you know, it's based on that. What seems
